The same issue for me. Yep, looks like gateway is not populated into hass at the time of notify service inits. 

Here is a possible way to fix it: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/38c57944fa1353e6bb1f0e3ba3187b86010f1e9d/homeassistant/components/netgear_lte/notify.py#L19. So just don't check the gateway in `get_service`, pass `hass` object into `SMSNotificationService` and check the gateway during the `async_send_message` call. Actually, I found a lot of components do the same.

Anyway, it will be nice to find the reason of this race condition.

review_comments:
The correct fix is to load the notify platform via our discovery helper `async_load_platform` after the gateway is set up in `async_setup_entry` in the init module.

This notify platform should not be set up via a platform config.

> The correct fix is to load the notify platform via our discovery helper `async_load_platform` after the gateway is set up in `async_setup_entry` in the init module.
> 
> This notify platform should not be set up via a platform config.

Thanks @MartinHjelmare . The current SMS notify is using platform config, but I would like to add a new one that does not require config. Can you point me to a sample notification that does not use config?

The tibber integration is one example. :+1: 

The webostv integration is even better as it has a guard in `async_get_service` for missing discovery info, so that it's not possible to set up the integration from an old platform config.
